calls.head: Fresh legs vs. tired ones
calls.body: The Penguins played last night and get no rest before this one. Teams in that spot usually get the worse of the chances, so we expect the Stars to control more of the play than they usually do.

calls.head: The Stars’ power play outclasses the Penguins’
calls.body: On the power play, Dallas is the league’s best, but Pittsburgh is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Every penalty the Penguins take could cost them.

calls.title: Dallas had the better chances
calls.plain: The Stars made the better chances on the power play, as the gap between these two suggested, but the goals came out even. On the scoreboard: Dallas 0 for 3, Pittsburgh 0 for 2 on the power play.
calls.said: the Stars’ power play would make more chances than the Penguins’
calls.beyond: Dallas has one of the league’s stingiest penalty kills. Even by those standards, this was a dry night: Pittsburgh’s power play created 0.2 expected goals per 60, against their usual 6.6 (about 5.6 against Dallas) and a league average of 7.7. A team strays this far about once every 150 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

DAL.head: We gave Dallas a 65% chance, and they delivered.

PIT.head: We gave Pittsburgh only a 35% chance, and it went the way we feared.

surprises.head: Jake Oettinger stole one with a shutout
surprises.body: Oettinger stopped all 33 shots, worth 3.2 expected goals. That is more than Dallas’s winning margin. Starting goalies have a night this good about once every 100 starts. Most starters don’t get one a season.

story.head: Oettinger shuts out the Penguins
paras: Joel Kiviranta scored the only goal of the game midway through the second.

The Stars were outshot 33-23, but their looks were better, and the chances came out about even. The Penguins hit four posts and came up a goal short. Jake Oettinger was perfect for the Stars, 33 saves on 33 shots, and Artūrs Šilovs stopped 22 of 23 at the other end. The Stars moved to 15-6-2, second in the Central, while the Pens dropped to 7-14-2, still last in the Metropolitan.
